method: lsctl text injection into the dev build; DeepSeek judge

scenarios.name: Founder interview: intro, basics, flowchart, sequence diagram

checks.them: Let's do something visual. Can you draw a flowchart of how a chat message goes from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen in our app?

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of a chat message from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.adopted: ViewModel sends the message, backend streams over SSE, ViewModel updates StateFlow, screen collects and renders
card.heard: draw a flowchart, user taps send → streamed reply on screen
card.say: I'll draw it top to bottom. The user taps send, and the ViewModel sends the message to the backend. The backend streams the reply back over SSE. Each piece goes into the ViewModel, then into StateFlow, and the screen collects it and shows the text as it arrives.
card.type: draw@chat message flow: flowchart TD ⏎ A[User taps send] --> B[ViewModel] ⏎ B --> C[Backend] ⏎ C -->|SSE stream| D[ViewModel] ⏎ D --> E[StateFlow] ⏎ E --> F[Screen shows text]
card.then: Next, I can explain what happens if the connection drops mid-stream.

checks.them: What happens in that flow if the network drops halfway through the reply? Add it to the diagram.

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of a chat message from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.adopted: ViewModel sends the message, backend streams over SSE, ViewModel updates StateFlow, screen collects and renders
card.constraints: ["If the network drops mid-reply, the ViewModel keeps received text, marks it incomplete, reconnects and continues from the last piece"]
card.heard: what happens if the network drops mid-reply, add it to the diagram
card.say: If the stream breaks, the ViewModel keeps the text it already has and marks the reply as incomplete. Then it reconnects and asks the backend to continue from the last piece it received. The screen shows a small "reconnecting" state, so the user knows the answer is still coming.
card.type: draw@flowchart: flowchart TD ⏎ D[ViewModel] -->|stream breaks| G[Mark reply incomplete] ⏎ G --> H[Reconnect with last piece] ⏎ H -->|continue| C[Backend]
card.then: Next, I can explain how the backend avoids sending the same piece twice after a reconnect.

checks.them: Good. Now a different one: draw me a sequence diagram of login, including what happens when the access token expires and the app refreshes it.

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of a chat message from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.adopted: App logs in, gets access and refresh tokens, sends the access token, refreshes once on 401 and retries
card.constraints: ["If the network drops mid-reply, the ViewModel keeps received text, marks it incomplete, reconnects and continues from the last piece"]
card.abandoned: ["ViewModel sends the message, backend streams over SSE, ViewModel updates StateFlow, screen collects and renders"]
card.heard: now a different one: sequence diagram of login with token refresh
card.say: Okay, a new diagram for login. The app sends the credentials to the backend, and the backend returns an access token and a refresh token. The app stores them and uses the access token on later calls. When a call comes back as expired, the app refreshes the token once and retries the call.
card.type: draw@: sequenceDiagram ⏎ participant App ⏎ participant API ⏎ participant Auth ⏎ App->>Auth: login (credentials) ⏎ Auth-->>App: access token + refresh token ⏎ App->>API: request with access token ⏎ API-->>App: 401 token expired ⏎ App->>Auth: refresh (refresh token) ⏎ Auth-->>App: new access token ⏎ App->>API: retry request with new token ⏎ API-->>App: 200 response
card.then: Next, I can explain how the app makes sure only one refresh runs when several calls fail at once.
